pages.text: This is {name}. {name} is a little green turtle with a warm sun on its round shell. The sun dips behind the hill, and the meadow quietly gets ready for sleep. The quiet evening smells of warm grass and flowers. "Good evening, little meadow," the little turtle whispers gently. And the meadow rustles back, ever so softly.

In the meadow lives one special little bud — the moonflower. All the other flowers opened long ago, but this one still sleeps, curled up like a small green lantern. {name} knows this little bud best of all in the meadow. "I wonder what you are dreaming about?" the little turtle thinks. The bud says nothing, but its silence is warm and cosy.

Every evening {name} comes and settles down beside the bud. "Maybe tonight?" the little turtle wonders softly. But the flower keeps sleeping, and that is all right. "Sleep as long as you need," {name} whispers gently. Waiting can be quiet and soft, like waiting for a good dream. There is no hurry here at all.

"Come play by the stream!" call the little ducklings. But {name} smiles gently and stays beside the flower. Waiting here is lovely too. "I will stay here, beside the flower," {name} answers quietly. "All right! We will splash a little and come back," the ducklings say cheerfully. And it is so quiet and good beside the little bud.

So that the waiting is never dull, {name} listens to the crickets. The little turtle closes its little eyes for a moment, to hear even better. Chirp-chirp, chirp-chirp they sing in the tall grass. It is the softest evening song. It drifts closer, then farther, like a gentle little swing. "You sing so nicely, little crickets," the little turtle whispers.

The first little star blinks on in the sky. {name} looks up and counts: "One…" The little star twinkles, as if saying a soft hello. The little turtle smiles back at it. And then waits for the next one to shine. The evening grows even gentler.

"Two… three… four…" {name} counts the stars as they come out one by one. "Five…" the little turtle whispers very softly. Every new little star is like a gentle light high above. The sky slowly wraps itself in a blanket of stars. Counting stars is so pleasant that little eyelids grow a bit heavy.

Warm night dew settles on the blades of grass, and they glisten like tiny beads. {name} gently touches one — cool and soft. The little drop trembles and catches the starlight inside. "How pretty you are," the little turtle whispers to the dewdrop. The blades of grass smell of freshness and quiet sleep.

"Don't be sad, little bud," {name} whispers softly. And the little turtle begins to tell the flower the kindest tale of all — about the stars that dance above the meadow. The words flow softly, like warm water. In this tale the stars twirl slowly and are never in a hurry. The little bud listens quietly — and everything feels warmer still.

The moon comes out from behind a little cloud, round and silver. It peeks over the meadow, as if it too wants to hear the tale about the stars. "Come in, Moon, and listen too," {name} whispers warmly. The moonlight settles on the grass softly, like a thin, thin cover. And the tale grows quieter still.

A gentle breeze sways the grass: swish-swish, swish-swish. {name} nestles cosily by the flower and breathes slow and deep. Breathe in — it smells of grass; breathe out — it smells of night. The little shell keeps the day's warmth, and that feels so snug. Waiting feels so calm. The evening rocks the meadow slowly and gently.

The bud stirs ever so slightly. {name} goes still and watches wide-eyed. It seems as if the flower has softly sighed in its sleep. "I am here, right beside you," the little turtle whispers. The little heart beats gently and gladly: tap-tap. Maybe the flower is dreaming something very lovely.

And then, on one warm quiet night, a wonder begins. Petal by petal the flower starts to open — slowly, slowly, as if waking from a dream. {name} holds very still, watching without a single blink. Each petal unfolds softly, like a tiny wing. "Sweet waking, little flower," the little turtle whispers tenderly.

The flower opens just for the one who knows how to wait. Its petals shine with a soft silver light. The light is gentle, so gentle, and does not dazzle little eyes at all. It smells of dew, of night, and of something very tender. {name} watches, and its little heart fills with warmth. "How beautiful you are," the little turtle breathes softly.

The silver glow spreads softly across the whole meadow. The grass, the dew, and the little turtle's shell all shimmer in the gentle moonlight. Everything around grows tender and warm. {name} looks around slowly: so much soft light everywhere! Even the crickets hush for a moment at such beauty. And then they sing on — even more tenderly than before.

The whole meadow lights up, as if someone lit little stars right in the grass. The little lights sway gently together with the grass. {name} smiles quietly: the loveliest things bloom for those who know how to wait. "Here it is, our wonder," the little turtle whispers to the flower. And the whole night begins to feel like a kind, kind tale.

The crickets sing very, very softly now. The breeze rocks the grass like a cradle. {name} gives a sweet yawn under the flower's soft glow. Little eyes blink slower and slower. The night strokes the meadow with warm silence. How cosy it is to doze beside the flower.

{name} snuggles down cosily in the soft grass beside the flower. The grass beneath the shell is soft as a little pillow. The glow wraps around the little turtle like a warm silver blanket. Its little eyes grow very heavy. Thoughts turn slow, warm and sleepy. "Good night, little flower," the little turtle whispers, barely audibly.

The moonflower shines soft and gentle, watching over sleep. The flower seems to whisper back: "Sleep now, I am near." {name} closes its little eyes to the crickets' lullaby. The breathing grows even and calm, like a quiet song. The meadow is so calm and warm. And sleep comes softly, like a petal settling on the grass.

The stars twinkle, the moon shines, and the flower glows soft and low. {name} drifts sweetly to sleep, its little heart all warm inside. The meadow breathes calmly, and the night breathes along with it. The little turtle dreams of something silver, gentle and very quiet. Good night, patient little heart. May moonflowers bloom in your dreams.
